title: 20.1 A 3.5×3.5mm2 1.47mW/ch 16-Channel MSS-CMOS Heterogeneous Multi-Modal-Gas-Sensor Chip Stack
problem: Miniaturized multi-channel gas sensors with low power are needed for wearables, ingestible biomedical devices, and smart tags, but traditional gas sensors separate transducers from CMOS via wiring, requiring large packaging; prior MEMS-CMOS stacks lack multi-gas capability and scalability.
motivation: Wearable health monitoring, ingestible diagnostics, and food freshness detection require compact, power-efficient multi-modal gas sensors; heterogeneous integration enables 16-channel densification within tight form factors.
method: Heterogeneous MEMS-CMOS stack integrating Membrane-type Surface-stress Sensor (MSS) transducers on top of CMOS analog frontend and digital readout; 16-channel architecture with 1.47mW/channel power on 3.5×3.5mm2 footprint.
key_novelty: First demonstration of multi-modal gas sensing via MSS-CMOS heterogeneous stack at 16-channel density, proving compact form factor and low per-channel power enable deployment in wearables and ingestible devices.
contributions: Heterogeneous MSS-CMOS integration enabling compact sensor stack without external wiring
Multi-modal gas sensing capability (responsive to multiple gas types)
Low per-channel power (1.47 mW/ch) suitable for wearable and battery-constrained applications
baselines: Traditional wired gas sensors, prior single-modal MEMS-CMOS stacks (refs 1-2)
limitations: Sensitivity, selectivity, response time, and detection range for specific gases not discussed; comparison with state-of-the-art gas sensors not provided.
primary_theme: Compact heterogeneous multi-modal gas sensor stack
